scope: Kiosk setup hold lifecycle around the existing NetworkManager worker, authenticated shared lease client and setup admission without resuming a saved profile conflict.

validation.client_clippy_note: Existing warnings in other client files remain; no diagnostic mentions the changed network files. This was not a warnings-denied client run.
validation.kiosk_feature_check: engine-client --no-default-features --features pi-kiosk-gpu --all-targets, host compilation only; existing extracted libseat/libinput development metadata under target/ota-host-tools supplied through PKG_CONFIG_PATH. No system packages installed.
validation.kiosk_feature_check_note: Existing unreachable-pattern warning in vendored Slint LinuxKMS backend. This is a type check, not a linked/deployed kiosk client or new image.

properties_exercised: Denied setup admission performs no automatic scan or connection mutation. A lost admission response still triggers a bounded release attempt with the same capability.
Closing the panel keeps protection while the existing worker rolls back. Renewal continues during delayed cleanup; release follows rollback completion.
Renewal failure closes the command channel, lets the existing transaction cancel and rollback, then releases. It does not drop the connection future mid-trial.
Mode Off leaves an independently disabled radio untouched while setup-protected allows ordinary saved-profile management. Wireless-ready remains a distinct actual radio result.
A profile conflict permits setup with a confirmed live radio but remains suspended after renewal/release. Rejected, uncertain or unmatched radio commands still refuse admission.
The shared client reuses its capability, requires a root peer before writing it, bounds framing/deadlines and rejects malformed, incomplete, unconfirmed and Ethernet-only setup replies.

The real shared client exchanges Admit/Renew/Release with the real coordinator and fake radio inside a root user namespace. It preserves profile suspension and detects lost temporary ownership after service restart.
Both Pis ran the manager and shared-client fixtures as UID 1000 using only private state, sockets and fake D-Bus/radio backends. Device boot identities stayed unchanged.

limits: No kiosk client, image, service, live network setting, root/boot/data partition or watchdog changed. No reboot or deliberate live radio failure was performed.
Setup hold integration requires the matching device service image. It has not been physically exercised through the UI on either Pi, and existing prepared bootstrap kits predate this work.
Expected setup profile changes remain conservative conflicts; finishing setup does not silently accept their baseline. Automatic policy needs explicit resume until that coordination is implemented.
The root interoperability check uses a user namespace and fake radio, not root access or native radio control on either physical Pi.
Clock code uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME for renewal scheduling and response-age checks, but this checkpoint did not physically suspend a device to qualify that behavior.
Deployment holds, supported SSH idle classification, daily scheduling, signing/feed, downloader, install policy and end-to-end OTA qualification remain outstanding.
